summary: Iteration 42 — Selfie-only attendance + community_manager role + RBAC. Backend 14/14 PASS. Frontend RBAC enforcement is COMPLETELY BROKEN due to a logic bug in rbac.js (prefix match on /console matches every /console/* path). All roles see the full admin sidebar and can reach forbidden pages via direct URL. Rider UI shell is correctly stripped of the blocking CheckInGate; topbar/bottom-nav/punch button all present. Result: sales, community_manager, stock_keeper all see the full admin sidebar (Finances, Livreurs, Zones, Produits, Stock, Statistiques, Historique pointages, etc).

Same rbac.js bug: direct nav to /console/finances or /console/produits as sales user is NOT redirected to /console — the forbidden page loads normally. canAccess('sales','/console/finances') returns true because of the /console prefix bug.

After login, the on-boarding tour modal 'Visite guidée' (backdrop + card) appears at page center and prevents interaction with the topbar 'Pointer' button. Clicking topbar-punch via Playwright (even with force=True) does not open the AttendancePunchModal because the tour overlay captures focus. The modal does open after tour dismissal (not re-verified end-to-end here).

Clicking data-testid='rider-punch-btn' did not reveal a punch-modal element in DOM in the automated run (possibly conditional on camera stream / state). Rider shell itself is correct: topbar, bottom-nav, 5 tabs (Courses/Carte/Historique/Performance/Profil), no blocking CheckInGate.
React hydration warning: <span> cannot be a child of <option> in PeriodSelector.jsx line 96. Not blocking but noisy in console.

The data-testid slug normalisation strips accents incorrectly: 'Rôles & permissions' -> 'nav-rles-et-permissions' (lost 'o'), 'À approuver' -> 'nav--approuver' (double dash), 'Aperçu' -> 'nav-aperu'. The replace(/é/g,'e').replace(/è/g,'e') does not cover ô/à/ç/É.

action_items: FIX /app/frontend/src/lib/rbac.js canAccess(): iterate PATH_ROLES keys sorted by length DESC (longest-prefix wins) OR require exact match (recommended). Current implementation: `for (const key of Object.keys(PATH_ROLES)) { if (path === key || path.startsWith(key + '/')) return ... }` — the '/console' entry at the top of the map always wins for any '/console/xxx' path. Suggested fix: `const keys = Object.keys(PATH_ROLES).sort((a,b)=>b.length-a.length); for (const key of keys) { if (path === key || path.startsWith(key + '/')) return PATH_ROLES[key].includes(role); }` and/or just use exact match for leaf routes.

After rbac fix, re-verify: sales must NOT see Finances/Livreurs/Produits/Zones/Statistiques; CM must NOT see Caisse/Livreurs/Produits/Stock/Finances/Sessions-caisse; direct URL /console/finances for sales must redirect to /console.

Investigate rider-punch-btn click → AttendancePunchModal not rendering in DOM (may be a conditional on getUserMedia availability — ensure modal element is present regardless of camera stream so test can detect it).
Fix on-boarding Visite guidée so it doesn't block the topbar Pointer button on first visit (either lower z-index or allow interactions with the topbar).
Fix <span> inside <option> hydration warning in /app/frontend/src/components/shared/PeriodSelector.jsx line 96.
Normalise sidebar nav-testid slugs to handle ô, à, ç, É (not just é/è).

rca_of_the_issue: File: /app/frontend/src/lib/rbac.js, function canAccess (lines 65-78). Bug: `Object.keys(PATH_ROLES)` returns keys in insertion order; the first key is '/console' with roles [manager, sales, stock_keeper, community_manager]. The loop uses `path.startsWith(key + '/')` which matches every '/console/<x>' path against the '/console' entry FIRST, returning that permissive list before any specific entry (e.g. '/console/finances':[manager]) is ever tested. Reproduction: login as sales (agent1@dinastore.ci/Agent123!), observe sidebar contains nav-finances/livreurs/produits/zones/statistiques; navigate browser to /console/finances → page loads instead of redirecting. Mitigation: `const keys = Object.keys(PATH_ROLES).sort((a,b)=>b.length-a.length);` before the for-loop, OR change to exact-match: `if (path in PATH_ROLES) return PATH_ROLES[path].includes(role); return false;` (plus a special case for '/console/clients/:id' prefix routes).
